title: Space Rogue
build: Origin Systems' two-sided disk, G64 images of side 1 (SHA-256 f8f4bdd5…) and side 2 (944b0898…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection (orientation.md)

records.c: The processor port: the intro runs with $34 (all RAM, its pictures and font under the ROMs) and banks the I/O and the KERNAL in ($36) for the hardware, the loads and the interrupt
The block copiers' source pointer (put_colour_block, put_matrix_block); nothing in the intro sets it, since nothing calls them

The block copiers' height in rows; never set in the intro

The dissolves' destination: the shown buffer's page

The high seven bits of the dissolves' 15-bit shift register, Y holding the low eight: bits 0-4 pick a page of the 8 KB bitmap, bits 5-6 the pixel pair in the byte. It starts at $7FFF, shifts right with taps $60 into this byte, and stops when it comes back, so every nonzero value comes once
The drawing buffer's page, $40 or $C0: print_char, the scrolls and unpack_picture draw there, and show_drawn shows it
The cursor's character row, 0-24
The cursor's column, 0-39
The text window's left column, where a new line starts
The text window's right column: a character that would go past it starts a new line first

print_text's pointer (into the digits or the ordinals), low byte
print_text's pointer, high byte
The most characters read_line takes: 11 for a name, 16 for an answer
The chosen question's answer in manual_questions, a pointer (find_question)
The answer's address, high byte
The question's page in the Sunracer Owner's Guide
The question's paragraph on that page
The question's sentence in that paragraph

The source pointer's high byte

The destination pointer's high byte

Not a variable: the operand of BIT $E8 at $6ADE, a byte scan_keys branches into as an INX ($6AE1)
The KERNAL's IRQ vector, pointed at irq_body ($6A60) so the interrupt also works while the KERNAL is banked in for a load
The IRQ vector's high byte

The BRK vector's high byte
The KERNAL's NMI vector, pointed at the RTI at $6A5A, so RESTORE does nothing
The NMI vector's high byte
colours_to_ram's patched STA at $71A8 was left here, the page after its $0C00-$0FFF staging buffer
Not data: BIT $1EA5 at $7017 hides LDA $1E (show_drawn, $7018) in its operand
Not data: BIT $40A9 at $7014 and at $7067 hides LDA #$40, the entries show_4000 ($7015) and clear_4000 ($7068)
The $4000 buffer's screen matrix ($6000-$63E7); clear_drawing's patched STA at $7075 was left pointing here after clearing the bitmap below

The intro's first instruction, at the start of INTRO: sets up the interrupt and the line table, loads FONT and SPACE, clears the $4000 bitmap, turns on the multicolour bitmap with white colours, unpacks the star field into the $C000 buffer and shows it, copies it to the $4000 buffer, shows that and goes to the Old or New prompt
load_inline's argument: load to $F200, then the file name "FONT" and a zero
Loads "SPACE" to $B700
load_inline's argument: load to $B700, then the file name "SPACE" and a zero
With the files in: clears the $4000 bitmap, sets the bitmap mode, shows the $4000 buffer, whitens the colour RAM and puts up the star field in both buffers
Banks the I/O and the KERNAL in ($01 low bits %110, RAM at $A000), keeping A
Banks all RAM in ($01 low bits %100), keeping A

Loads the file named after the JSR: two bytes of load address (low, high), then the name ending in a zero, and returns past the zero. LOAD runs from device 8 with secondary address 0, so the file goes to that address whatever its header says, and is retried until the KERNAL reports no error; the caller's $30/$31 are kept in the patched loads at $68B9 and $68BD
The name's length, patched in by $6884
The name's address, low byte, patched in by $688C
The name's address, high byte, patched in by $6893
The load address's low byte, patched in by $6868
The load address's high byte, patched in by $686E
The caller's $30, patched in by $6850 and put back on the way out
The caller's $31, patched in by $6855
Clears any key waiting, waits for the interrupt to put one in key ($3C), clears it again and returns it in A
Sets key ($3C) to $FF: none waiting

A wait of about 0.86 seconds that a key ends early (the key stays in $3C). clear_key leaves A at $FF, so the caller's A makes no difference: the 26-cycle loop always runs 255 + 254 + ... + 1 = 32,640 times (848,640 cycles), and the interrupt adds its share
Prints the character in A at the cursor, keeping A, the flags, and X and Y (put back by the patched loads at $68FD and $68FF)
The caller's X, patched in by $68F7
The caller's Y, patched in by $68F4

Draws character A (bit 7 ignored) into the drawing buffer at the cursor: RETURN ($0D) starts a new line, $08 and $7F rub out the character before the cursor, and a character that would pass the window's right edge starts a new line first. Its 8 bytes are copied from FONT ($F200 + 8 × the character) into the bitmap cell, and the cursor moves on a column
The cursor row's offset in a bitmap, low byte, patched in from char_row_offsets ($694C); the ADC adds the column's offset to it
The cursor row's offset, high byte, ORed with the drawing buffer's page ($6954)
The character's address in FONT, low byte, patched in by $693A
The character's address in FONT, high byte: built from character × 8 and then $F2 added ($6942)
The bitmap cell's address, low byte, patched in by $6961
The bitmap cell's address, high byte, patched in by $6968

Rubs out the character before the cursor: prints a space at the cursor, steps back two columns, prints another and steps back one, leaving the cursor a column to the left (the BPL at $6985 lands on the next instruction either way)

Moves the cursor to the window's left column on the next row. Past row 24 it scrolls the drawing buffer's rows 1-24 up a character row instead (7,680 bytes) and clears only the first 64 bytes of the bottom row, 8 of its 40 cells: $69E5 loads Y = 1 where the 320-byte row needs 2
new_line's scroll source, low byte, set to $40 (row 1 starts 320 bytes in)
new_line's scroll source page, the drawing buffer's plus one, stepped on each page
new_line's scroll destination page, the drawing buffer's own, stepped on each page
The bottom row's address, low byte, set to zero
The bottom row's page, the drawing buffer's plus $1E (row 24 starts 7,680 bytes in)
The byte counter new_line's two loops count down

With interrupts off, points every vector at the intro's own handlers: a raster interrupt at line $50 with CIA1's interrupts off; the NMI and BRK vectors at the RTI at $6A5A (it also writes that address to $FFFC, which a reset never reads from RAM); the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at irq_body and the hardware one ($FFFE) at irq. Then clears the key, sets up the SID and banks all RAM in
An RTI: the NMI (RESTORE) and BRK do nothing
The raster interrupt as the hardware vector enters it, with all RAM banked in: pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL's entry would and goes on into irq_body

The raster interrupt as $0314 enters it, the KERNAL having pushed the registers: saves $01, banks the I/O in, acknowledges the raster, scans the keyboard (a new or repeating key goes to key without bit 7), counts the frame in $3D, runs the effect player and returns

Scans the keyboard matrix itself; returns C set with a key's code in A when a key is new or repeating, C clear otherwise. CTRL and the two SHIFTs are read first and masked out of their rows; the first key held, row 7 down to row 0 and bit 7 down to bit 0 within a row, is numbered 8 × the row's place + the bit's and looked up in key_codes, or key_codes_shifted with either SHIFT, CTRL keeping only the low five bits. A held key repeats 36 frames after it went down, then every 6. Port A is left an input
BIT $E8 hides an INX ($E8) at $6ADF: the first pass skips it and the BCS at $6AE1 lands on it, so X counts the row's released keys from bit 7 down to the one held
The last key's number, $FF for none
Frames left before a held key first repeats: 30 from a new key
Frames left before the next repeat: 6
For each row in scan order (7 down to 0), the bits of its modifier keys, ORed in so they never count as a key: CTRL in row 7, right SHIFT in row 6, left SHIFT in row 1
CTRL's bit from row 7, zero while it is held
Right SHIFT's bit from row 6, zero while it is held
Left SHIFT's bit from row 1, zero while it is held

The 64 keys' codes in scan order (row 7 bit 7 first): ASCII for letters (lower case), digits and punctuation, $0D for RETURN, $7F for DEL, $08 for the left-arrow key, $1B for F1, $09 and $0A for the cursor keys, and $80 for the keys the intro ignores, which arrive as 0 since the interrupt keeps seven bits
The same with a SHIFT held: capitals, the symbols over the digits, $0B for cursor up and $08 for cursor left

Wipes the window's character rows X to Y off to the left: the rows slide a cell at a time (wipe_left_step), the two buffers taking turns so that each flip shows one more cell, until the window's width has gone
Moves character rows $36 to $38 - 1 of the drawing buffer one cell left within the window, clearing its right-hand cell
Wipes the window's character rows X to Y off to the right, as wipe_left does to the left
Moves character rows $36 to $38 - 1 one cell right within the window, clearing its left-hand cell
Scrolls the window's character rows X to Y up and away, two pixel lines a step, showing each step with its colours (show_drawn_colours) and catching the other buffer up
Moves the window's pixel lines up two through the line table, then clears the bottom two (clear_line)
Clears pixel line X of the window in the drawing buffer
Scrolls the window's character rows X to Y down and away, two pixel lines a step, as scroll_up does upwards; nothing in the intro calls it
Moves the window's pixel lines down two, working from the bottom up, then clears the top two
Copies the colours to the colour RAM, then runs copy_matrix; nothing calls it

Copies 8 pages, a buffer's $2000-$27FF (screen matrix and colours), from page A ORed with $12 to the same place in the other buffer. Only dissolve_in calls it, with A = $1E, which makes the source $E000 whichever buffer is shown
copy_matrix's source page, patched in and stepped
copy_matrix's destination page, the source's with bit 7 flipped
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture to the $C000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer (copy_shown) and its colours to the colour RAM, so the next page of text is drawn over the same picture
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture, bitmap, screen matrix and colours ($28 pages), to the $C000 buffer
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer
The picture copy's source page, patched in and stepped
The snapshot shows this STA's page left at $68, after a copy to the $4000 buffer
The picture copy's destination page, patched in and stepped
Sets $34/$35 to column A × 8
Returns character row A's offset in the drawing buffer, low byte in A and high in Y (with the buffer's page ORed in), X = 0; the caller's X is put back in the LDX at $6E55
row_address's caller's X, patched in by $6E47
Fills the colour RAM, $D800-$DBFF, with 1 (white), interrupts off
The page of white_colours' STA, stepped from $D8; the snapshot shows it left at $DC
Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the colour RAM at column X of row Y (colour_rows), the source advancing by the width each row; nothing in the intro calls it
put_colour_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_colour_block's destination, high byte

Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the drawing buffer's screen matrix at column X of row Y (matrix_rows), the source advancing by block_stride ($66) each row; entered at $6EC2 for the $C000 buffer and $6EC6 for the $4000 one. Nothing in the intro calls it
put_matrix_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_matrix_block's destination, high byte
Builds the pixel-line table at $EB00 (low bytes) and $EC00 (high): for each of the 200 lines, (line / 8) × 320 + line mod 8
The offset build_line_table is working on, low byte; it leaves $1F40 (8,000) in the pair
The offset build_line_table is working on, high byte
Each character row's offset in a bitmap, 320 × the row, a word each for rows 0-24 (print_char, row_address)
char_row_offsets read from one byte on, for the high bytes (X = 2 × the row)
Each row's address in the colour RAM, $D800 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_colour_block)
colour_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes
Each row's offset from a buffer's page to its screen matrix, $2000 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_matrix_block)
matrix_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes

Turns the multicolour bitmap on ($D011 bit 5, $D016 bit 4), with the bitmap at the start of the VIC's bank and the screen matrix $2000 into it ($D018 = $80), and the background black. Its read-modify-write of $D011 also writes back bit 7, which reads as bit 8 of the beam's line and writes bit 8 of the raster compare: run while the beam is on line 256 or later, it moves the interrupt from line $50 to $150 (336), which no frame reaches, and the interrupt stops for good
Shows the $C000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Shows the $4000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM
Shows the drawing buffer (show_drawn) and copies its colours to the colour RAM: the step after each page of the story is drawn

Shows the $C000 buffer (the VIC's bank 3, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = 0) and makes $4000 the drawing buffer. The BITs that follow hide two more entries in their operands, show_4000 (LDA #$40) and show_drawn (LDA $1E). Sets $3A to the shown buffer's page, $12 to its screen matrix's and $1E to the other buffer's
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, show_4000's entry
Shows the $4000 buffer (the VIC's bank 1, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = %10) and makes $C000 the drawing buffer; the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $7014
BIT $1EA5: its operand is LDA $1E, show_drawn's entry
Shows the drawing buffer, the shown one becoming the drawing buffer: the flip after each page is drawn; the LDA $1E here is the operand of the BIT at $7017
Clears the drawing buffer's bitmap, 32 pages; the BITs that follow hide entries for the $4000 buffer ($7068) and the $C000 one ($706B). Only clear_4000 is called
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, clear_4000's entry
Clears the $4000 buffer's bitmap ($4000-$5FFF), called once at the start; the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $7067
BIT $C0A9: its operand is LDA #$C0, an entry at $706B for the $C000 buffer
The page clear_drawing's STA writes, patched in and stepped; the snapshot shows it left at $60

Brings the drawing buffer's picture onto the shown one a pixel pair at a time in a scattered order: after copy_matrix, a 15-bit shift register visits every pixel pair of the 8 KB bitmap once (dissolve_lfsr). Nothing in the intro calls it
The pixel pair from the drawing buffer, patched into this ORA by $70BF
The four pixel pairs of a multicolour byte, left to right
The bits each pixel pair leaves alone, the complements of pixel_masks
Fades the shown picture to black a pixel pair at a time, in the shift register's scattered order: before the second picture is shown ($7D8D) and at the end of the story ($824C)
The complements of pixel_masks again, for dissolve_out

Unpacks the picture packed at page A into the drawing buffer: a byte below $80 is a count and the next byte is repeated that many times; $80 plus a count is followed by that many bytes to copy; a zero is followed by the border colour, which is stored too, written to $D020, and ends it. A whole picture is a buffer's bitmap, its screen matrix at +$2000 and its colours at +$2400

Copies the shown buffer's colours (its +$2400) to the colour RAM: first to $0C00 with all RAM banked in, then on to $D800 with the I/O in, since the RAM under the KERNAL and the colour RAM cannot both be seen at once
colours_to_ram's source page, the shown buffer's plus $24, stepped
colours_to_ram's staging page, from $0C, stepped
The staging page read back, from $0C, stepped
The colour RAM page written, from $D8, stepped
Silences the SID's three voices, turns the filter off and the volume up (15), and sets up the effect player and the masks
Starts sound effect A (0-4; others are ignored) on voice 1, copying its settings from the effect tables to $80-$8C with interrupts off

The effect player, run by the interrupt every frame: starts each repeat of the effect's note (frequency, envelope, waveform, gate), moves the frequency by the step each frame, releases the gate at the release point and silences the note when its frames run out. Below that, a second sound left in from a shared driver slides $74/$75 up 2 a frame towards $72/$73 and would play it while no effect is, but drone_mask is zero, so in the intro it never sounds
Each effect's starting frequency, low byte, for effects 0-4
Effect 4's starting frequency, low byte, set by tone ($7428)
Each effect's starting frequency, high byte: $10, $18, $01, $80, and effect 4's
Effect 4's starting frequency, high byte, set by tone ($742B)
Each effect's frequency step per frame, low byte
Each effect's step, high byte: effect 0 falls by $80 a frame, effect 1 rises by $80, effect 2 falls by 2, effect 3 rises by $600, effect 4 holds
Each effect's attack and decay
Each effect's sustain and release
Each effect's waveform with the gate: noise ($81) for effects 0, 2 and 3, pulse ($41) for 1 and 4
Each effect's note length in frames: 32, 48, 128, 32, and effect 4's
Effect 4's note length, set by tone and silence ($7425)
The frames-left count at which each effect releases its gate
How many notes each effect plays: three for effect 1, one for the rest
Plays effect 3, rising noise, as the airlock cycles, and waits for it
Plays effect 1, three rising tones, for the alert
Plays effect 0, two 18-frame silences and effect 0 again, as the PRINCESS BLUE explodes
Plays effect 0, falling noise
Plays effect 2, noise falling slowly for 128 frames, after the explosion
Plays effect A and waits until it has finished or a key is pressed; if a key is already waiting it plays nothing
Sends morse_text with tones (the elements' routines in morse_routines) until its closing zero or a key, which is then cleared: the distress beacon of the first story page
The Morse character's address, low byte, patched in and stepped
The Morse character's address, high byte
The element routine's address, low byte, patched into this JSR from morse_routines
The element routine's address, high byte

The distress call, SOS SOS PLAY ULTIMA SOS SOS: $AE a dot and $AD a dash, $A7 a short gap between the letters of SOS, $A0 a gap between the other letters and $AF a gap between words (the five codes are morse_symbols)
morse_text's closing zero, where distress_call's patched load at $7363 was left
The five Morse characters distress_call looks up, in morse_routines' order: dot, dash, gap, word gap, short gap
The Morse elements' routines, a word each: morse_dot, morse_dash, morse_gap, silence_18 and silence_4
morse_routines read from one byte on, for the high bytes (Y = 2 × the element)
A dot: a 2-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
A dash: a 6-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
The gap between letters: 6 frames of silence
18 frames of silence (effect 4 at frequency 0): the gap between Morse words and the pause in explosion_sound
4 frames of silence, the gap between the letters of SOS
A tone at frequency $3864 lasting A frames
A frames of silence: effect 4 at frequency 0

Asks "What is your name?" on row 21 of the shown buffer and reads up to 11 characters into line_buffer. The BVS at $7435 always skips the copy and show below it: bit 6 of $3A is set for either buffer ($40, $C0)
Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "What is your name? _"
The name goes at column 24 of row 21, empty to start with, 11 characters at most

Reads a line into line_buffer at the cursor: printable keys are kept and echoed up to line_limit, DEL and the left-arrow key rub out the last, and RETURN ends it once something has been typed, rubbing out the cursor and closing the line with a zero
Handles a key for read_line: rubs out on $08 or $7F, otherwise stores and prints it if the line has room

The check for an old game: unpacks the star field into the drawing buffer and shows it, picks one of the 32 manual questions from the frame counter ((frame_count AND 31) + 1), asks it and compares the answer, folded to capitals, with the word. Returns C clear when the first four letters match (the rest is not read), C set when not
Steps through manual_questions to entry A (1-32), each record ending in a zero, copies its four numbers to $2C-$2F and leaves $2A/$2B at its word
Prints A in decimal, one or two digits, at the cursor, building the text in number_text
Stores digit A at ($27) in ASCII and moves on a byte
print_number's digits, up to two and a closing zero (the byte before is never used)
Divides A by the divisor at decimal_divisors + X by repeated subtraction: the quotient in Y and the remainder in A
The divisors, 10 and 1
Prints word A of ordinals ("first" to "tenth")
Prints the text at ($27) up to its zero

Prints the manual question on rows 8-12 of the shown buffer, "Look at the second paragraph on page 1... What is the third word in the first sentence?", and reads the answer, up to 16 characters, on row 14

The answer at column 0 of row 14, up to 16 characters, the window from column 12
"first" to "tenth", each ending in a zero, for print_ordinal

The 32 questions for an old game, each the page, paragraph, sentence and word in the Sunracer Owner's Guide, then the word in capitals and a zero. The first, page 1, paragraph 2, sentence 1, word 3, is SCOUT ("Your Sunracer scout ship embodies..."); the pages run from 1 to 46
Copies 36 pages from $B700, SPACE and what follows, to page X; nothing in the intro calls it
copy_space's source page, patched to $B7 and stepped
copy_space's destination page, patched in from X and stepped

Waits for a key while drawing the cursor at the cursor's column as a space and an underscore in turn; returns DEL, the left-arrow key's $08, RETURN or a printable character, and waits on through the others
Prints the text after the JSR, through the patched load at $7894, up to its zero, and returns to the instruction after the zero

random_state's 16th byte, the start of each sum and the low byte of the count

The orders' closing zero, where print_inline's patched load at $7894 was left when the snapshot was taken
